The test image shows soybean plants at soil level with:
- Dark brown/black necrotic tissue at the stem base near soil line
- Dead, dried brown stems throughout
- Some orange-brown discoloration at the soil line
- Whole plant death visible

This pattern strongly suggests a root/stem base rot. Top candidates: **Phytophthora** (dark chocolate-brown lower stem), **Charcoal_Rot** (gray with black specks near soil), or **Rhizoctonia**.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows:
- Very dark brown-to-black necrotic tissue at the stem base at soil level
- Completely dead, dried plants
- Reddish-orange exposure of internal stem tissue at soil line
- Ground-level shot showing stem rot/collapse near the soil

The Phytophthora reference confirms the pattern: dead plants with brown/wilted leaves still attached, dark discoloration at stem base extending from the soil line — matching the "dark chocolate-brown stem discoloration extending from below soil line upward" description. The test image captures the late-stage stem base collapse characteristic of Phytophthora root rot.
